newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle Atlantis docks with Russia's Mir.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle Atlantis docks with Russia's Mir.

text.p: The U.S. shuttle Atlantis docked with Russia's Mir space station on Tuesday night, bringing fresh supplies and a change of crew for the orbiting outpost.
The two craft linked up at 10:54 p.m. EST (0354 GMT) as they soared 247 miles (398 km) above Russia, southeast of Moscow. It was the fifth time the shuttle had docked at Mir.
The hatches between the spaceships were due to swing open about 90 minutes after the docking, allowing astronaut Jerry Linenger to take the place of current U.S. Mir resident John Blaha.

Blaha, a 54-year-old Vietnam veteran, is due to return to Earth aboard Atlantis on Jan. 22 after 128 days in space. During his stay on Mir he peformed more than 60 scientific experiments, including one to grow wheat in space.

Linenger's tour of duty is scheduled to end in May, a month before the birth of his second child is expected. The astronaut, who turns 42 this week, has accepted that a shuttle delay could make him miss the birth.
Linenger will be the fourth U.S. astronaut to live aboard Mir, as NASA learns to work with Russia before embarking on the international space station project later this year.
